The program pulls every `name <- value;` assignment out of the text in order, so the surrounding prose is ignored. It runs each one, treating the right-hand side as either an integer literal or another variable's current value, and then prints the final values.

```python
import sys
import re

def main():
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    env = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*<-\s*(-?\d+|[A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*;')
    for m in pattern.finditer(text):
        target, src = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+', src):
            val = int(src)
        else:
            val = env.get(src, 0)
        env[target] = val
    a = env.get('a', 0)
    b = env.get('b', 0)
    t = env.get('TMP', 0)
    print(f"a ?= {a}; b ?= {b}; TMP ?= {t};")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
